title: policy.json: ecosystems
description: Which build-system ecosystem applies to which paths (HITLD-910, HITLD-911): profiles are data (manifests, lockfiles, version sources, folders to skip, caches) and never run anything; the commands for a project's paths appear only here, in ecosystems.use, as owner configuration. The mapping is explicit: nothing is detected at run time. `hitld work check` refuses an unknown profile, a version-source file that is not a repository path and a skip folder with a separator or `..`.

use.description: The profiles in use, each with the path globs it applies to (* within a segment, ** across segments). When several entries' globs match one file, the most specific glob wins, as for release.packages.

profile.description: A built-in profile (npm, pnpm, yarn, cargo, go, pip, uv, poetry, maven, gradle, bundler, composer) or one of ecosystems.profiles.

paths.description: The paths it applies to, as globs relative to the repository root with / separators. A folder takes a wildcard: web/** for everything under web, since web alone matches only a file named web. `hitld work check` refuses a glob with a backslash, a `..` segment or a leading `~`, one ending in /, and a glob without a wildcard that does not name a regular file in the checkout (a folder, a symbolic link or a path that is not there), naming the web/** form: such a glob matches nothing the owner meant, and passing it silently is what the check is for.

commands.description: The install, build, test and publish commands for these paths, each a list run in order through the shell. This is the only place an ecosystem's command may appear: owner configuration, never agent input, as env.worktree_setup is. In this release hitld validates them and runs none of them; env.worktree_setup and the merge checks still run what they run today.

install.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell

build.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell

test.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell

publish.description: Publish the paths' package to its registry.
publish.x-hitld-executes: each entry is run through the shell

commands.x-hitld-executes: each list's entries are run through the shell

profiles.description: The project's own profiles, as data like the built-in ones: a new ecosystem, or one that extends a built-in profile and replaces some of its lists. A profile never holds a command.
